A large pharmaceutical company has conducted extensive animal testing of a new drug for the treatment of advanced prostate cancer. The chief of research and development recommends that the company now submits an investigational new drug (IND) application in order to start clinical trials. Which of the following statements is most correct regarding clinical trials of new drugs?
options: Phase 1 involves the study of a small number of normal volunteers by highly trained clinical pharmacologists
Phase 2 involves the use of the new drug in a large number of patients (1000–5000) who have the disease to be treated under conditions of proposed use (eg, outpatients)
Phase 4 involves the detailed study of toxic effects that have been discovered in phase 3
Phase 2 requires the use of a positive control (a known effective drug) and a placebo

A.stem: Which of the following would probably not be included in an optimal phase 3 clinical trial of a new analgesic drug for SEVERE pain?
options: A positive control (current standard analgesic therapy)
Double-blind protocol (in which neither the patient nor immediate observers of the patient know which agent is active
A group of 1000–5000 subjects with a clinical condition requiring analgesia

A.stem: Which of the following statements about the testing of new compounds for potential therapeutic use in the treatment of hypertension is most correct?
options: Animal tests cannot be used to predict the types of clinical toxicities that may occur because there is no correlation with human toxicity
Human studies in normal individuals will be done before the drug is used in individuals with hypertension
The degree of risk must be assessed in at least 3 species of animals, including 1 primate species
The animal therapeutic index must be known before trial of the agents in humans

Z.T. is a 53 year old male patient who was started on warfarin (5 m.g. o.d) one month ago following an episode of deep venous thrombosis in his left femoral vein which he developed during when he was admitted for acute complications of T.B. that was the cause of the above admission. He is visiting your anticoagulation clinic for international normalized ratio (INR) monitoring. The INR is 1.2 (desired target 2-3). A doppler ultra sound of the affected region shows no change in clot size from baseline. Swelling of the left lower limb has also not reduced. He reports that he is faithfully taking his anti-TB medication and attends TB clinic.
a) Describe the drug-drug interaction that is likely to be at play in Z.T. (2 marks)
b) Describe two interventions that you could initiate to overcome or avoid the above interaction (2 marks)

C.stem:
S.K. is a 16 year old male patient admitted to your in-patient unit with altered consciousness and several episodes of seizures. His caregivers report that he drank a bottle-full of insecticide whose container they carried. He is producing copious secretions from his mouth and nose and eyes, has emptied his bowels and bladder several times and vomited. Wheezing is audible on chest auscultation. The musculoskeletal examination reveals profound weakness in his arms and legs; muscle twitches are also present. His respiratory muscle effort is also diminished. On admission the heart rate was 51 beats per minute and the respiratory rate was 10 breaths per minute. Other vital signs are within the normal range. After establishing that his airway is clear and instituting supportive care to stabilize vitals and fluid status you are able to identify chlorpyrifos (an organophosphate) as the active agent.
a) Describe the mechanism of anticholinesterase insecticides (both organophosphates and carbamate) (3 marks)
b) Outline the clinical effects of anticholinesterase insecticide poisoning on S.K. based on Ach activity on each of the following receptors
Muscarinic (5 marks)
CNS receptors (mixed type) (2 marks)
Nicotinic-neuromuscular neurons (2 marks)
Nicotinic-sympathetic (2 marks)
c) State the antidote that is likely to improve symptoms of muscle weakness in S.K. (1 mark)
